source.title: Messiah, HWV 56 — Hallelujah
source.edition: Unknown: the Mutopia catalogue does not identify a source edition

bars.description: Bars 1–94 once. The source separates SATB, winds, brass, timpani and four string staves; no independent double-bass part or keyboard realisation is invented.

end.basis: The fresh final-candidate pitch-energy overlay shows the final D-major chord from about 250.5 s through 256.5 s, with its pitched bands disappearing by about 256.7 s. Later transfer noise keeps global RMS active to the 265.06 s file end; it is not encoded as an extra nine seconds of sustained orchestral/choral notes. This is a measured display boundary, not a claimed physical key or bow release.

endpoints.basis: First and last score-pitch windows inspected against the candidate spectrogram: musical opening around 3.08 s follows transfer transients, and the closing D-major chord begins around 250.5 s. Its measured pitch-energy display end is recorded separately from surface noise.

provenance: Mutopia 459 supplies the complete Hallelujah chorus, 94 bars in 4/4, with source-defined orchestral staves and four SATB choral staves. Combined-source MIDI is used; timbral MIDI patches are not interpreted as recording instrumentation.
The source catalogue labels its underlying edition Unknown. Separate double-bass pitches and realised continuo are not encoded and are not invented.
This historical recording has transfer noise; its RMS tail is not automatically evidence of sustained music. No aural review is claimed.
